Theme

theme.json and semantics.json are the look; lib/ui/theme.ts reads them for every component.

The theme is the upstream gallery's: a graphite page (paper in light appearance), cards and insets, one citrus accent, compact controls with a pointer and roomier ones on a touch screen. It is two JSON files — base tokens in theme.json and cross-platform semantics in semantics.json, following the design-semantics standard — plus the module that reads them, and every component takes its colors, radii, typography, motion and depth from there. No component writes a color of its own.

Files

FileWhat it holds
theme.jsonBase tokens: colors (light / dark and shared), the three radius-* layer lengths (plus radius), in shadcn's cssVars shape
light.tokens.json, dark.tokens.jsonStandalone W3C DTCG 2025.10 Format files resolved per appearance at the pointer tier (in-file aliases, 6-digit hex fallbacks) for Figma Variables (Light/Dark modes), Tokens Studio, and Style Dictionary v4; static snapshots as shipped
DESIGN.mdGenerated Google Labs DESIGN.md (alpha) specification for coding agents, compiled from DTCG sources and the pointer-tier light/dark resolutions; static snapshot as shipped
semantics.jsonSemantic layer in DTCG names: 7 style groups (typography, dimension — with the four control dimensions under dimension.control — shape, state, transition, motion (three timings plus the state fade), controls), elevation (the shadow scale, per appearance) and finishes (shared + sparse light / dark), referencing tokens with {token}
lib/ui/theme.tscolors, finish, shape, font, style, control, focusRing and alpha, read reactively from theme.json and semantics.json

Installation

add theme writes theme.json, light.tokens.json, dark.tokens.json, DESIGN.md, lib/ui/semantics.json and lib/ui/theme.ts, the data of the theme nsh-ui.json records (theme-shadcn writes shadcn's into themes/shadcn/). init writes the same files and also points each nsh.json at theme.json. In a monorepo they live under packages/ui. Every component depends on it.

light.tokens.json, dark.tokens.json and DESIGN.md are generated outputs: import .tokens.json into Figma Variables as Light and Dark modes, Tokens Studio, or Style Dictionary v4, and let coding agents read DESIGN.md for the theme's tokens and design rationale. Because they describe the theme as shipped, editing theme.json or semantics.json later does not update them.

Colors

theme.json is a shadcn theme: cssVars.theme holds the radii and the accent's raw values, cssVars.light and cssVars.dark hold the same semantic keys for the two appearances. The core keys are shadcn's (background, foreground, card, popover, primary, secondary, muted, accent, destructive, border, input, ring, chart-1 … chart-5, sidebar*). Upstream adds the roles the gallery needs:

RoleUse
inset / raisedA surface inside a card, and a control on the card
field / inputAn input's well and its edge
line / borderHairlines inside insets, and the edge of a card or control
hover / faintThe pointer's wash, and the quietest text
brandThe accent as ink
track / knobA switch's track when off, and a switch's knob; sliders and progress bars read their preset's track role
info / warn / upThe tones beside the accent; a data loss reads destructive
brand-tint, info-tint, warn-tint, destructive-tint, up-tintThe same tones as fills behind text (negative trend reuses destructive-tint)
inverse / inverse-foreground / inverse-brandA toast's and a tooltip's reversed surface, its text and action; quieter ink is finish.inverse.foreground

colors maps the roles a component names onto those keys:

Read a role where it is drawn (in JSX, a draw, or an effect): the getters read the token then, so they follow the appearance.

Finishes

A finish is light and depth: what a surface is filled with, and how it sits above what is behind it. There are fourteen — eleven layers a component can be drawn on, and three states — and a finish states the same fields in every theme: background, foreground, shadow, material, gradient, backdropFilter, the three border colours, the pressed pair and elevation. A field a theme leaves out is not missing — it takes a neutral value, written once in the base token set (tokens/base/style.shared.tokens.json) and compiled into every theme's semantics.json: material: null (no platform material), backdropFilter: "none", elevation: null, gradient: null (flat), no colour of its own on the top or bottom edge, and the pressed pair null (pressing only dims). In the DTCG sources those neutrals are written "none" in the finish group's $extensions, since a token's $value cannot be null; a token a theme writes wins over it. semantics.json keeps finishes.shared (fields identical in both appearances, referencing {token} so NSH's token() handles light/dark switching) plus sparse finishes.light and finishes.dark overrides, and finish.<role> merges them and resolves every {token} (including oklch(from {card} l c h / 0.78)) for the active appearance.

RoleUse
cardA surface that holds content: a card, a section
insetA surface sunk into its host: a field, a track, a well
raisedA surface above the page: a button at rest, a chip, a pill
overlayA surface the page floats over: a menu, a popover, a select's list
modalA surface the page waits for: a dialog, a sheet
inverseThe reversed surface: a toast, a tooltip
glassA control over a photo
accentThe brand's own surface: a filled button, a switch that is on
knobThe thumb a control moves: a switch's knob, a slider's handle
hoverThe pointer's treatment of the surface under it
pressedThe press's treatment of the surface under it
disabledA control that cannot act

Every finish states a foreground — the ink that sits on it — so a component needs no fallback, and shadow names the parts of the theme's scale (["{shadow.edge.surface}", "{shadow.sm}"]) instead of writing one: elevation("md") gives the same values on its own. A theme that paints flat leaves gradient out and gets null, so the component draws no background image.

The material says what the platform's own glass should be: null (every theme but the glassed ones, which state "none" and compile to null), or apple — { glass: "regular" | "clear", tint } — which rides inside finish.<role> as glassEffect and glassTintColor, so a spread of the finish carries it. ios, macos and windows are props, not style keys, which platformMaterial(role) returns for the view that draws the finish:

Both follow selectTheme and the appearance, and with material: null the view is drawn as before. The library's own popovers, hover cards, toasts, the editor's find bar and a glass carousel arrow spread it; the popups of Menu, Select and Popover on nsh/base take only popupStyle, so there the glass keys apply and the platform props do not.

The apple theme fills in material.apple: glass, overlay and raised carry { glass: "regular" } (Liquid Glass on iOS and macOS 26+), and every other finish is a flat fill with a hairline edge. The material theme uses Material 3 Expressive tonal surfaces, circular corners, 8/10/10% state layers, press ripple (state.ripple: true), and material.android.elevation on elevated surfaces. The winui theme uses WinUI 3 (Windows 11) fill and stroke tokens, 4/8-point circular corners, Segoe UI Variable, Consolas, double focus rings, timing motion, underline tab and box-underline field indicators, and material.windows blur on glass, overlay and inverse. nativeTheme() from theme-native picks the theme of the platform the app runs on — Apple's on iOS and macOS, Material on Android, WinUI 3 on Windows, and the NSH Gallery theme everywhere else:

init --theme apple builds the app on Apple's palette; --theme native builds it on the NSH Gallery theme and installs both, for nativeTheme() to choose between at run time. On macOS 26+ an explicit macos.backdrop wins over glassEffect, so apple states none; it states ios.backdrop as the blur for iOS before 26.

Windows' Mica is not a finish: it is the window's own backdrop in nsh-desktop (Windows 11 maps it to Mica or Acrylic, macOS to a visual effect material), set once by the app in nsh.json and shown through surfaces whose fill is translucent:

Radii

theme.json's cssVars.theme block defines three corner radii, one per layer: radius-control (in-page elements: fields, rows, chips, badges, wells, colour areas, keycaps), radius-container (cards, menus, popovers, rich tooltips, list panels, toasts) and radius-modal (dialogs, sheets, drawers). shadcn's own radius slot equals radius-control. shape resolves each role reactively via token(), and buttonCorner(size) reads controls().button.corner ("control" or "full" capsule):

ThemecontrolcontainermodalButtons
default, shadcn81214control
solid-glass111420control
apple81226capsule
material41228capsule
winui488control

A surface inside another takes a concentric corner from its outer one: rounded(outer, inset) gives outer − inset, never below 0. rounded() also puts the corner on with shape.curve ("continuous" or "circular"):

Reading the theme

focusRing(offset) is the shared keyboard outline: the muted ring edge and a 3-point halo of ring at 30%. hovered() is the pointer's fill, the hover token (plus stateLayer("hover") when state.overlay.hover > 0). alpha(color, a) is a color-mix of that color with transparency. colors, finish, shape and style() are reactive: read them where they are used.

Override from nsh.json

An app's nsh.json sets the look in two places, and the two do not merge:

Key in nsh.jsonWhat it setsWhen it is read
"theme"the path to theme.json: every base token — colours, the radius-* tokenson each read, at runtime — so setTheme, setThemeOverrides, shape reach it
"tailwind"the app's own class strings: colors, fontFamily, spacing, radius, …when the app is built, into the class strings — no component here reads it

Components take their look from "theme": colors, finish, shape and font read the tokens where they are used. "tailwind" shapes class names — which this library writes too (bg-muted, text-sm, h-8) — but it is fixed at build time, so nothing in it can follow setTheme. NSH's theme tokens has the rule in full.

A colour named in "tailwind" wins over the token of the same name. With "colors": { "primary": "#3366ff" }, every bg-primary in the app draws blue — pagination's selected page, a data table's move indicator — while colors.primary in JSX stays the theme's citrus. One name, two colours, and the panels drawn by class are the ones that differ. Set the role in "theme" instead.

The theme file stays complete: copy it, then edit. A shadcn slot it leaves out falls back to shadcn's neutral (see Colors), and semantics.json names tokens with {token}, so both appearances need the same set.

Add a colour the app's own classes use (both appearances — a token in one alone is not a token):

Change a role: primary in cssVars.light and cssVars.dark. Change a radius: radius-control, radius-container or radius-modal in cssVars.theme (keep radius equal to radius-control) — every corner follows them: shape.* and rounded() in the styles, and rounded-(--radius…) in the classes, this library's and the app's own alike. Fonts are the app's own: see Fonts.

Fonts

A theme owns no font: none of the shipped themes declares a family, and one type scale (sizes and line heights) serves them all, so switching themes never reflows text. Each theme still states its own weight and letter spacing per role. Text names no family of its own; it takes the app's font-sans, and monospaced text (the font-mono class, code in a Text) takes font-mono — this library writes the generic monospace where it needs a monospaced face. Each of the 7 typography composites carries fontFamily: "system-ui" because DTCG requires the field, but the library never reads it. The user's system font size scales every size.

Set the app's families in the cssVars.theme block of its own theme.json:

NSH takes the first family of the list that is not a generic one (system-ui, sans-serif, monospace …), and a list of generics alone is the system's own font. That is why this library writes monospace: the system's monospaced font, not a font called "monospace".

A font file is the app's. Import it in TSX — the import registers it before the first frame, and its value is the family name the file declares, not the file name — and name that family in the theme:

The side-effect import is deliberate: TypeScript drops an import whose value is unused, and the font with it, when the theme names the family as a string. A weight or an italic is a file of its own, registerFont(bytes) reads one the app did not ship, and the fallback after the app's family is what NSH draws for a family it cannot find — see NSH's fonts.

This library distributes no font files: add theme writes JSON and TypeScript and names no family.

Restyling

Edit the sources; every component follows. Change a brand color in cssVars.light and cssVars.dark, a radius in cssVars.theme, a shadow part in the DTCG shadow group, a gradient, style group or material in the theme's tokens/ files. Keep the keys: components and finishes refer to them by name, and both appearances need the same merged finish shape — a finish you add states every field of its neighbours, and a value that follows the device is stated twice, pointer and touch, with the same keys — a theme that has its own device sizes writes them in tokens/themes/<id>/pointer.tokens.json and touch.tokens.json, and one that does not inherits the base set's.

  • Add the theme to an app with shadcn-nsh add theme (or let init do it); subsequent add runs key-merge missing entries into theme.json and semantics.json while keeping your values.
  • Replacing both files together rebrands the whole library; a key added upstream should be added here too.
  • The demos on this site can draw in an installed theme: the Demo theme switch in the nav (Default, shadcn, Solid Glass, Apple, Material or WinUI 3) writes the demo app's palette and loads the panels again. The list is apps/website/demos/palettes.ts; a demo reads the palette before it mounts, so its first frame is already the chosen theme. Every palette — its install command and every role it sets — has a page linked from Themes.
  • To change one component's look instead, edit its look function in the copied component; to change structure or API, edit the shell. See Customizing.
  • Maintaining this repository: edit the look in packages/ui (all of it is ours; a credit line in the header says where it began); port:check lists upstream's changes and bun run port:review marks them read. After editing packages/theme, run bun run registry:build and commit public/r.

Theme rules and decisions: docs/specs/design-semantics.md, docs/specs/theme-roles.md and packages/theme/README.md. Behavior and accessibility are nsh/base's: nsh.dev/elements.
